results.changes: -2 Mountain, +2 Island. The deck has 12 blue cards (Sokka, First-Time Flyer, Dragonfly Swarm) but only 12 blue sources, which is too few to cast a turn-2 Flyer or Sokka reliably. Moving to 14 blue sources fixes that while keeping 19 red sources for the red one-drops and Lessons. Islands also turn on Riverpyre Verge's blue mode. Land count stays at 21: the curve tops out at 3, and Abandon Attachments, Sokka and Tersa all smooth draws. Kicker gives a mana sink for flood.

No changes. The mana base already fits the plan.
Land count: 24 lands suits a landfall deck that also plays lands off the top with Traveling Chocobo.
Fetch lands: the 7 fetches (Fabled Passage, Escape Tunnel) each trigger landfall twice, and the 11 basics give them enough targets.
Green: 11 lands make untapped green on turn 1, and 20 make green overall.
Splashes: red (Full Bore) and blue (Spell Snare) each need only one pip. Each has 2 shocklands, 1 Verge and 2 basics, plus the fetches.
Rejected: the Temur triome, gainlands and surveil lands all enter tapped and would slow the aggressive curve.

Kept 24 lands, so no spells changed. The deck has a high top end (Deceit, Sunderflock), and Flamebraider, Ashling and Eclipsed Flamekin already smooth the draws, so 24 is right.
-1 Island, -1 Mountain, +2 Thundering Falls: it is typed Island Mountain, so it makes both colors and Eclipsed Flamekin can pick it up off the top four. It also turns on Riverpyre Verge's blue, and its surveil helps find the Elemental pieces. Blue sources rise to 19 and red to 18, which matters most for the double-blue cards (Wistfulness, Deceit, Sunderflock) and for casting Ashling with red on turn 2 and paying blue on turn 3.
Kept 2 Cavern of Souls naming Elemental, since every creature is an Elemental. More copies would leave Bounce Off and Burst Lightning with only colorless mana.

Kept 22 lands. With 8 mana creatures (Llanowar Elves, Bramble Familiar) and cheap Aang recasts, that count is enough. Blue was the weak color at 12 sources, even though 4 Doc Aurlock and 4 Floodpits Drowner want it on turn 2 and Aang on turn 3.
-2 Overgrown Farmland, +2 Starting Town: it enters untapped on turns 1-3 and makes any color, so it helps both turn-1 Elves and blue on turn 2.
-1 Plains, +1 Meticulous Archive: a Plains Island that turns on Hushwood Verge's white and Floodfarm Verge's blue, adds a blue source, and its surveil can set up Esper Origins flashback.
Result: about 15 green, 15 white and 15 blue sources, up from 15/15/12, with the shocklands and Verges unchanged.

results.changes: No changes. 22 lands is right for this low-curve aggro deck. Nothing costs more than 3 except kicked Burst Lightning, Ultimate Green Goblin makes Treasure, and the many discard outlets turn extra lands into value, so going below the 23.5 average is fine. Colors are balanced at 17 red sources (for Phoenix's RR) and 17 black sources (for 2-drop Elf and 1-drop Flail). The hybrid spells take either color. Blood Crypt and Haunted Ridge keep the early turns mostly untapped. Restless Vents earns its tapped entry as a menace attacker that also loots, which fits the discard theme. Razortrap Gorge often comes in untapped once this deck has dropped the opponent to 13 life.

Overgrown Tomb, Watery Grave and Breeding Pool were not Standard-legal in September 2025. I swapped them out: -4 Overgrown Tomb, -3 Watery Grave, -3 Breeding Pool, +3 Underground Mortuary, +2 Undercity Sewers, +1 Gloomlake Verge, +1 Hedge Maze, +2 Swamp, +1 Forest. The surveil lands also help fill the graveyard for Spider-Man and Overlord. The basics and the Swamp/Forest/Island-typed duals turn on both Verges and cut down on tapped lands.
I kept 22 lands. Four Llanowar Elves plus ten mill-to-hand effects (Town Greeter, Dredger's Insight, Cache Grab) make up for the high curve, so no spells changed.
Sources: about 19 black (for Massacre Wurm BBB and Bringer BB), 16 green plus Elves, and 9 blue for the six Spider-Man and Lotuslight cards. Starting Town stays as the Town that triggers Town Greeter's lifegain.

-1 Mountain, +1 Plains. Ten two-drops need white on turn 2: Kíli, Dáin's Company, Thorin and Giott, plus Lightning Helix. 14 white sources was thin for that, so the swap moves the split to 17 red / 15 white. 17 red sources still support turn-1 Dwarven Mauler and Burst Lightning. I kept 22 lands, which suits this low curve. Leyline Axe can start on the battlefield and the Lonely Mountains work as a mana sink. The Lonely Mountains stay because 12 Equipment plus Dáin's Axe token usually let them enter untapped. The fast lands (Inspiring Vantage) and Sundown Pass already cover the early and late turns of an aggro deck. No spell changes.

Kept 26 lands. This is a control deck that wants to hit seven mana for Jeskai Revelation, and Consult the Star Charts scales with land count. The draw spells offset the risk of flooding.
-1 Mountain, +1 Thundering Falls: adds a blue source while keeping red. It is still a Mountain for Sunbillow Verge and an Island for Cori Mountain Monastery.
-1 Hallowed Fountain, +1 Sacred Foundry: red was the thinnest main color. It rises from 10 to 11 real sources, plus the 4 Great Halls, for early Lightning Helix and Flashback. Blue (15) and white (18) stay deep.
Black splash is unchanged: Watery Grave, Godless Shrine and 4 Great Hall, with Resonating Lute as backup. Great Hall's any-color mana covers Inevitable Defeat since it's an instant.

No changes. The mana base is already right. 23 lands matches the format average and suits an explore deck that wants lands to hit off the top. There are 20 green and 20 black sources, which covers Jadelight Ranger's GG on turn 3 and Sheoldred's BB on turn 4. That count treats each Pathway as one face. Blooming Marsh handles the early turns and Deathcap Glade the later ones. Overgrown Tomb and the four basics turn on Woodland Cemetery. Boseiju and Takenuma add utility at almost no cost. Takenuma's channel gets cheaper with Sheoldred in play.

-1 Swamp, +1 Fountainport. The deck is mono-black and its curve tops out at three, so 22 lands is right; no spells change. The deck makes Treasures, which can be sacrificed to Fountainport to draw. Fountainport's Fish tokens are fodder for the sacrifice outlets, and each token sacrificed drains through The Sackville-Bagginses. That makes a second Fountainport a strong mana sink. Soulstone Sanctuary stays as another late-game sink. 19 Swamps among 22 lands still cast Bloodghast's BB on turn 2 reliably, and every other spell needs only a single B.
Soulstone Sanctuary stays because it is a reliable mana sink.

results.changes: -1 Mountain, +1 Shivan Reef. 20 lands is right for this low curve: nothing costs more than 3, and the deck has learn and looting effects. Red is already covered by all 20 lands. Blue was the weak spot at 15 sources, which is thin for a turn-1 Stormchaser's Talent and for Boomerang Basics. The 4th Reef raises blue to 16 sources while staying untapped. Three Mountains plus the Vents still turn on Riverpyre Verge's blue mode. The rest of the mana base stays as it was.

-1 Swamp, -1 Mountain, +2 Blood Crypt. The land count stays at 18, which is right for a Death's Shadow deck that also runs 4 Bauble and 4 Street Wraith. Six basics was too many for a deck that wants to lose life. Every fetch can find Blood Crypt, so the extra copies make it easier to hit both B and R early: Thoughtseize/Spoils/Shadow and Ragavan/Bolt/Thud all want turn-1 mana. Paying 2 life to untap a Crypt also helps shrink Death's Shadow's drawback. Keeping 2 Swamp and 2 Mountain leaves fetchable basics against Blood Moon and Wasteland effects. All 10 fetches still find either color.

-1 Mountain, +1 Swamp. The deck is mostly black: Bloodghast needs BB on turn two, there are lots of black one-drops, and Persist and Flare of Malice are black. Red is only a light splash for Looting, Bolt and Phoenix bestow. After the swap there are 17 black sources out of 18 (counting Boggart Bog) and 12 red, which is still plenty for one-mana red spells. The extra basic Swamp also turns on Spymaster's Vault untapped and is another fetch target. I kept the land count at 17 plus the Trawler MDFC. The curve is very low, Archon is meant to be reanimated rather than hard-cast, and Looting and the sacrifice draw spells smooth out draws. I kept all 6 fetches because they give Bloodghast landfall triggers and add to the graveyard. Raucous Theater's surveil and Vault's connive both fit the graveyard and sacrifice plan.

No changes. The 19 lands plus 4 Turntimber Symbiosis land faces give about 23 land drops. Utopia Sprawl, Talismans and Spawn tokens add ramp on top. Utopia Sprawl has 10 Forest targets: 5 Forest, 2 Stomping Ground and 3 fetches. Green comes from 14 lands plus Sprawl and Talisman. Kozilek's Return's single red is covered by Stomping Ground, the fetches, Talisman and Sprawl naming red. 8 Temple/Labyrinth plus Cavern and Talismans cover the {C}{C} costs. The 10 colorless 7-drops support Labyrinth. The fetches also put a land in the graveyard for Emrakul's discount."}

-2 Forgotten Cave, +2 Mountain. The deck has to make 5 mana for Creative Technique or 2 red for an early Tibalt's Trickery as fast as possible, and a land that enters tapped costs a full turn. The 8 horizon lands already give enough card draw from lands, so the tapped cycling lands were the weakest part of the mana base.
The land count stays at 37. That is far above the format average on purpose: lands are skipped by Creative Technique and by cascade, so a high land count keeps the nonland pool focused on Apex Devastator and Call Forth the Tempest. No spell copies were changed.
Kept as is: Ancient Tomb, City of Traitors, Gemstone Caverns, Lotus Petal and Simian Spirit Guide as fast mana. Urza's Saga also stays, since it fetches Lotus Petal. The deck only ever needs red mana, and every land except Tomb, City and Saga provides it, which is plenty.

+1 Scalding Tarn, -1 Thoughtseize. The deck is three colors and needs to find U, B and R early (Buried Alive at 3 mana, Looting and Lava Dart on red, cantrips on blue), so 15 lands was slightly thin even with Petals and Rituals. 16 lands is still low for the format but fits this cantrip-heavy list. Tarn, like Delta and Mire, can fetch every dual here, which gives 7 fetches and better access to all three colors. The duals stay as they are: Badlands and Volcanic double as Mountains for Lava Dart's flashback. Thoughtseize was the least essential spell, and its life cost stacks badly with fetches and Force of Will.

-1 Island, +1 Tolarian Academy. This deck routinely has a lot of artifacts in play: 11 mana rocks, Cams, Servants, Extruders, Moxite, and artifact lands. With that many, Academy makes a large amount of blue mana. That pays for Cam activations, hard-cast Force of Will and Time Walk.
Land count stays at 15. That is right for a deck with 11 fast-mana artifacts, slightly below the 15.4 average.
Blue sources remain ample: 4 Volcanic Island, Seat of the Synod, Academy, and 5 fetches that all find Volcanic.
Red sources are untouched, which matters for the 8 red one- and two-drop creatures and 4 Pyroblast.
One basic Mountain stays as a fetch target against Wasteland.
The artifact lands and Urza's Saga stay because they feed Welder, Engineer, Extruder and Mox Opal. Saga can also tutor Grindstone.

-2 Shattered Landscape, -1 Sheltering Landscape: their cycling costs need black or green, which this deck can't make. They also tap for colorless and fetch a basic that enters tapped. +2 Ash Barrens fixes either color and can cycle for {1} into an untapped basic.
-1 Plains, +1 Mountain: there are eight red one-drops (Bolt and Firebolt) plus red flashback costs, so this goes to 13 red and 13 white sources. That evens out the many turn-two {R}{W} plays.
Lands go from 19 to 18. Four Boros Garrisons already add extra mana, and the curve tops out at 4, so 18 is enough. The freed slot goes to a 4th Skyknight Legionnaire, another multicolored spell that returns the Eidolons.
Kept: the 4 Garrisons, which help pay for the flashbacks and the Eidolon loop, and the 2 Crags.

+1 Swamp, -1 Insidious Dreams. Living Death costs 5 with BB, and the deck needs to hit those land drops even with Rituals and Birds. 20 lands was slightly light, so I went to 21. Flood is cheap here because Putrid Imp can discard spare lands to fuel the graveyard. Insidious Dreams was the clunkiest spell, since it competes with Survival and Imp for discard fodder. Black sources go to 16, which supports turn-1 Ritual or Duress, Buried Alive and Living Death's BB. Green stays at 13 plus Birds for Survival. The painlands, City of Brass and Gemstone Mine stay as the untapped dual sources. White and red are never needed from lands, because Akroma, Nishoba and Squee are reanimated or discarded rather than cast.
